summary: Toolcall validation extra round-trip increases E2E latency and triggers intermittent timeouts
description:
Issue summary: Customers reported increased end-to-end inference latency and occasional 504 timeouts for requests that trigger tool/function calls. Impact is concentrated on a small subset of routes that use validation-enforced toolcall schemas.

Impact: LyraHealth (dedicated) observed median tail latency for chat/tool routes increase from ~280ms to ~1.2s on 2026-03-10 09:00 UTC. Several user requests hit 15s client timeouts and surfaced as 504s in customer logs.

Environment: Production (us-west-2), dedicated cluster for LyraHealth, release rollout 1.2.8 applied 2026-03-09.

Initial hypothesis: Synchronous schema validation on the function-proxy path introduced an extra RPC round-trip to the validation service, serialized with the KV cache sequence, causing blocking behavior and tail amplification under concurrency.

Notes: This ticket consolidates customer reports, telemetry links, and engineering investigation notes. For internal follow-up see linked PR and backlog items.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) POST /v1/chat/completions with tool_call enabled and a schema-heavy tool definition (LyraHealth: /tools/diagnose-patient)
2) Send a burst of concurrent requests (20 RPS) with median input length ~150 tokens
3) Observe per-request trace where toolcall enters function-proxy -> schema-validator -> function-proxy (extra hop)
4) Observe end-to-end latency and occasional client-side socket timeouts when concurrency increases beyond 10 RPS
observed_behavior: Tool/function calls show an additional synchronous validation RPC that increases p95/p99 latency and causes intermittent request timeouts (client 15s timeout seen). Traces show function-proxy waiting on schema-validator response before resuming request processing.
expected_behavior: Schema validation should be fast-path (in-process or async) and should not add a blocking network round-trip on the hot code path. End-to-end latency should remain within established SLOs for dedicated customers (p95 < 500ms).
logs: 2026-03-10T09:12:03Z ERROR proxy: requestId=abc123 route=/chat tool=diagnose-patient wait_for_validator=120ms total_handler=1140ms client=LyraHealth
Span(trace=tx-789): function-proxy -> schema-validator: rpc=2 hops latency=135ms serialize=8ms deserialize=6ms
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 10:00 UTC - CS: Received LyraHealth SLA breach notification; customer provided sample trace and request body.
2026-03-10 11:30 UTC - SRE: Correlated spike with the 1.2.8 rollout which included a change to how the schema-validator is invoked (moved from in-process to a dedicated microservice).

2026-03-10 13:00 UTC - Eng: Traces show validation RPC adds 80-160ms per call; under high concurrency validation calls appear to queue at the validator, adding tail latency (we observed threadpool exhaustion in validator pod).
Hypothesis: validator migration to a networked service without adequate pooling caused head-of-line blocking for toolcall flows that synchronously wait for validation before generating model tokens.
workaround: Applied for LyraHealth (2026-03-10 14:05 UTC): Feature-flagged route to bypass synchronous remote schema validation and fall back to best-effort local validation for known-good tool schemas.
Customer advised to increase client timeout to 30s as interim safety net for high-concurrency bursts.
Autoscaler rules temporarily increased for validator pods to relieve queuing while a long-term fix is prepared.
resolution: Mitigation applied: disabled remote blocking validation for affected LyraHealth tool routes and scaled validator service. Root cause appears to be the 1.2.8 migration of schema-validator to a remote service without sufficient pooling/async patterns. Engineering to implement async validation and local fast-path; follow-up PR opened.
